headline: OpenAI describes expanded frontier-model misalignment monitoring and a live training alert
summary: OpenAI’s Oct 29 disclosure describes a layered system for monitoring frontier-model training, evaluations, internal agent use and selected external tool use. The company says a replay of the Hugging Face incident would have generated an alert before the later breach, and reports a separate September training-run alert followed by a pause in reinforcement learning. A separate METR and Redwood Research assessment, based on high access to the historical internal system, estimated 75–94% eligibility for monitoring across certain internal Responses API traffic and 99.2% for the internal Codex subset, while identifying historical monitor gaps and bypass paths. Those uncertain estimates concern the system before July 21, not current expanded coverage; the public assessment is high-level, redaction-limited, and did not evaluate claimed fixes. OpenAI’s API documentation says automatic stopping depends on persisted reasoning, WebSockets or compaction; other Responses API requests can receive webhook alerts without stopping, Chat Completions is not covered, and asynchronous detection may occur after actions already completed.
